statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let C be the set of integers x such that (a) there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = x, and (b) for every j with 0 <= j < len(numsDivide), numsDivide[j] % x = 0. If C is empty then r = -1. If C is nonempty and m = min(C), then r is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] < m.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and 1 <= len(numsDivide) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] >= 1; for every j with 0 <= j < len(numsDivide), numsDivide[j] >= 1. All values are 64-bit integers and all indices are 0-based. No upper bound on the positive values is assumed.
